##### **Transcript**

Did you know you can build mobile applications in JavaScript and still include native Swift and Kotlin code? When I was building Skylight Social, the tick tock competitor built in the AT protocol, the team and I at this dot labs were tasked with building a native in app video editor. We use the Expo modules SDK to get it done. I've got a small demo project here. From here we're just going to run the command NPX create Expo module. We'll give it the local flag to let the generator know that we want the modules code located directly inside of our project, and then we just give it a name. My module. And we'll let that generate some initial boilerplate for us. Running that command will create a modules directory that will have my module inside of it, which includes some source code for Android as well as some source code for iOS and Swift. You can see here. The documentation for the Expo Modules SDK is pretty straightforward. Here's an example of what a simple column module would look like. You can see some custom function definitions here, and inside of those function definitions is the actual Kotlin code that we want to execute. There's a similar pattern here for our Swift code as well. I want to. We'll start by going into my Swift module and doing some customizations to the Hello function. And now that we're done with that, we're going to go into our Kotlin module and make a similar modification. Now, calling that functionality is very simple, we're just going to import our module. And now we can call those functions directly inside of our React markup. Alright, let's do a clean rebuild of our application. And justice like that, we're done. Here's our application running in an Android emulator with our custom Kotlin code being executed. Here's the same component running inside of an iOS simulator with our custom Swift code being executed. Now we have a single React Native application with custom Kotlin code and custom Swift code inside the same repository. How awesome is that?
